release_notes.headline_internal: ADR-002: ADV adopts a workflow hibernation lifecycle state (decision only, no code)
highlights: ADR-002 decided AFFIRMATIVE on architectural-shape grounds: ADV will let stale-but-open change and epic workflows complete and be recreated on demand.
Reversed from an earlier NEGATIVE verdict after the supporting cost measurement was found invalid — it was sampled immediately after a manual cleanup pass and omitted that cleanup as a variable.

Both previously-blocking preconditions recorded as resolved with call-site anchors: running-worker identity via bundle-generation parity (DEC-1), and the terminal race via a self-completing signal (DEC-2).
Epics identified as the clearest case and the leading phase-1 candidate: 40 running, zero ever closed, no routine close path exists.
rq-hib04 (signal-loss observability) promoted from standalone hardening to a blocking prerequisite — hibernation increases completion events, which is when buffered signals are lost.
Nine overturned assumptions catalogued in the ADR itself, including three claims asserted beyond their evidence that review caught and corrected.
New reference skill at ~/.config/opencode/skills/agent-temporal-lifecycle/SKILL.md — 8 sourced Temporal facts, 6 ADV-specific anchors, every external claim carrying a source URL.
Downstream implementation change addWorkflowHibernation created, carrying DEC-1, DEC-2, DDC1/2/6/8/10 and a mandatory rq-changeLifecycleState01 spec amendment.
